## Game
Game: Cube Cash Tycoon - Watch cubes roll down your conveyor, cash in, and buy droppers and speed upgrades to grow your tiny factory!
Core loop: Each player gets a bright plot with a dropper that spawns a 1-cash cube every 2 seconds onto a conveyor. The conveyor carries cubes to a collector at the end, and the server adds each cube's value to the player's Cash leaderstat and destroys the cube. Two buy pads sit off to the side of the walking area: a second dropper for 25 cash and a faster conveyor for 50 cash. Touching a pad with enough cash buys the upgrade once, so income climbs and the numbers go up.
Acceptance: The map (baseplate and the player's plot with dropper, conveyor, collector and two buy pads) is built from parts at startup and the 'map_built' counter is 1; The player spawns on their plot within a few seconds, and 'plot_assigned' is 1; 'cubes_dropped' increases within the first 2 seconds and keeps increasing roughly every 2 seconds; 'cubes_collected' increases as cubes reach the collector, and the Cash leaderstat rises; Touching a buy pad with insufficient cash does nothing; with enough cash it deducts the cost once and increments 'dropper_bought' or 'conveyor_bought'; The HUD shows the current Cash and updates as it changes; Walking from spawn does not trigger the buy pads accidentally, and the cube count stays under the cap; No errors or warnings appear in the output; At startup the plaza (stone tiles, fountain, lamp posts, trees) and 6 plots in a ring exist; 'plaza_built' is 1, 'themes_built' is 6 and 'map_built' is 1; Each plot has a distinct theme floor material and color plus 3-5 decoration props (lollipops, lava cracks, crystals, palm trees, neon strips, cacti), and no part is default grey; rails, dropper bodies and pads use theme colors; Players spawn in the plaza, not on a plot, and cubes_dropped stays 0 until a plot is claimed; Each free plot shows a glowing gate with a BillboardGui reading 'Claim <Theme> Plot'; Walking onto a gate claims that plot: the sign shows the player's name, the gate hides, 'plots_claimed' and 'plot_assigned' increase, and 'cubes_dropped' starts rising about every 2 seconds; A player who does not claim within 20 seconds is auto-claimed to the nearest free plot ('auto_claims' increases) and the dropper starts; ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades has 10 upgrades with unique ids, every requires id exists, and the first purchase (Dropper 2) costs 10; After claiming a plot, only the Dropper 2 pad is visible on that plot, with a billboard showing its name and '$10'; Within about 10 seconds of claiming, Cash reaches 10 and the Dropper 2 pad turns the plot accent color; Touching Dropper 2 with enough cash deducts 10 exactly once, the pad vanishes, the Silver, Speed 1 and Dropper 3 pads appear, and 'upgrades_bought' increments; Touching a pad with insufficient cash, or whose parent is not owned, does nothing and deducts nothing; After Dropper 2 is bought, two cubes spawn per drop cycle and 'cubes_dropped' rises faster

## Game files
ReplicatedStorage/CashInConfig.luau  -- CashInConfig: pure shared tunables for cash-in and purchase feedback.
ReplicatedStorage/Config.luau  -- Shared constants for Cube Cash Tycoon. Single source of truth for tunables.
ReplicatedStorage/ForgeChecksPlan.luau  -- ForgeChecksPlan: pure data describing the live playtest check plan.
ReplicatedStorage/ForgeTelemetry.luau  -- ForgeTelemetry: tiny counter API for generated games. ForgeProbe reports these counters.

ReplicatedStorage/NumberFormat.luau  -- NumberFormat: pure shared helpers for compact number display (no services, no side effects).
ReplicatedStorage/PlotThemes.luau  -- PlotThemes: shared config for the plaza, the 6-plot ring and the plot themes.
ReplicatedStorage/RebirthConfig.luau  -- RebirthConfig: shared tunables and pure helpers for the Rebirth feature (server and client).
ReplicatedStorage/TutorialConfig.luau  -- Pure shared tunables for the first-60-seconds tutorial.
ReplicatedStorage/UiTheme.luau  -- UiTheme: pure shared UI kit for the house Theme (no side effects, no server code).
ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades.luau  -- Upgrades: pure data for the dropper / ore tier / speed / cash multiplier tree.
ServerScriptService/CashInService.luau  -- CashInService: server-side owner of cash-in / purchase feedback.
ServerScriptService/DataService.luau
ServerScriptService/ForgeChecks.server.luau  -- ForgeChecks: Studio-only live playtest runner. Reads game state only.
ServerScriptService/ForgeProbe.server.luau  -- ForgeProbe: playtest error/telemetry collector for forge (Studio only).
ServerScriptService/ForgeTest.server.luau  -- ForgeTest: in-game test harness for the mubit-tester MCP server (Studio only). docs/TESTER.md.
ServerScriptService/Game.server.luau
ServerScriptService/JuiceService.luau  -- JuiceService: server side of the juice/polish pass.
ServerScriptService/LeaderboardService.server.luau  -- LeaderboardService: lifetime-earnings tracking, leaderstats guarantees and the in-world TOP TYCOONS board.
ServerScriptService/PlazaBuilder.luau  -- PlazaBuilder: themed plaza, plot decoration, claim gates and owner signs (all built from parts).
ServerScriptService/PlotBuilder.luau  -- PlotBuilder: builds the baseplate and six themed tycoon plots on a ring around the plaza, entirely from parts.
ServerScriptService/PlotClaimService.luau  -- PlotClaimService: themed plot claiming, auto-claim after timeout, release on leave.
ServerScriptService/RebirthService.luau  -- RebirthService: server-authoritative rebirth system (altar, remotes, multiplier, leaderstat).
ServerScriptService/TutorialService.luau  -- TutorialService: server owner of first-60-seconds tutorial state.
ServerScriptService/Tycoon.luau
ServerScriptService/UpgradeService.luau
StarterPlayerScripts/CashInFx.client.luau  -- CashInFx (client): cash-in popups, sounds, particles, HUD pulse, purchase confetti, spinning collector rings.
StarterPlayerScripts/ForgeTestAgent.client.luau  -- ForgeTestAgent: per-client actuator for the ForgeTest harness (Studio only). docs/TESTER.md.
StarterPlayerScripts/Hud.client.luau  -- Hud.client.luau: UI only. Shows Cash, a hint line, and toast messages from the server.
StarterPlayerScripts/JuiceFx.client.luau
StarterPlayerScripts/RebirthClient.client.luau  -- RebirthClient: client-only UI for the Rebirth feature (button, golden flash, banner, toast).
StarterPlayerScripts/ShopUi.client.luau  -- ShopUi.client: client-only shop panel (SHOP button + upgrade cards). Sends intent only.
StarterPlayerScripts/TutorialGuide.client.luau  -- TutorialGuide: client-only first-60-seconds guide (banner + bouncing arrow + beam).
StarterPlayerScripts/UpgradeFx.client.luau  -- UpgradeFx: client-only toast + corner label for upgrades. Sends nothing to the server.

## Feature request
Add executable checks and fix failures for: the SHOP button opens a panel listing every Upgrades entry with price and affordability, and buying Dropper 2 for 10 works once; the rebirth altar appears at 5000 cash or when all upgrades are owned, and rebirth applies the multiplier and resets cash and upgrades; the plaza TOP TYCOONS board lists Cash and Rebirths; the tutorial arrow and banner appear after the first claim and advance on the first purchase. Mark each feature verified when its checks pass.

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~10-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback should fire within a few seconds, and claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza. Otherwise the loop is never exercised.
- Keep tutorial text consistent with the actual flow (e.g. don't say "walk to a gate" if auto-claim happens within seconds).
- Feedback should be audible and visible: use verified sound ids from the shared asset table, not weak built-in rbxasset wavs. Add particles or ambient sparkle, and set the bloom threshold low enough that Neon parts glow.

## Luau and Roblox APIs
- The base place is empty: build the map from code (Instance.new Parts, Anchored = true, parented to Workspace).
- Get services with game:GetService("Players") etc.; use task.wait / task.spawn / task.delay, never wait / spawn / delay.
- Players.PlayerAdded can fire before your script connects in a playtest: also loop over Players:GetPlayers() once at startup.
- Wait for characters with player.CharacterAdded (and player.Character if already present); use WaitForChild with a timeout across the client/server boundary.
- ModuleScripts must return exactly one value (usually a table); require them by path, e.g. require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Config")).
- Create RemoteEvents on the server in one place; clients only WaitForChild them and handle nil after the timeout.
- Bump counters for key gameplay events with require(ReplicatedStorage.ForgeTelemetry).count("name", 1) (server only) so playtests can verify the core loop. Include counters for purchases and other branches that need verification.
- Count each telemetry counter in exactly one place (the module that owns the event). Duplicate count calls push once-only counters past their expected value; a counter at 2x its expected value (e.g. 12 vs 6) means a double init or double build, so check for it.
- Each builder/init function must be called exactly once from the entry script. If two modules both build the same thing (e.g. plaza and plot builders both building themes), assign ownership to one.
- Touched fires many times per touch: debounce per player (a per-player cooldown or
